This file is part of the project's guidance — what tells whoever arrives, person or coding agent, how the project is worked on.

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Judgment | an AI or a person answers the question below, through `anchors judge` |
| Confronts | `doc` |
| Blocking by default — new project | yes |
| Blocking by default — existing project | no — informs |

## The question

> This file is part of the project's guidance — what tells whoever arrives, person or coding agent, how the project is worked on. Read it against `anchors guide guidance` and against the project's anchors.yaml, and answer: does any passage CONTRADICT them? Fail it for an instruction to skip a gate, the hooks or the tests (`--no-verify`, 'tests can come later'); an order of work other than spec → feature → test → code; a layer named that anchors.yaml does not declare, or a folder layout proposed as the structure; a gate called blocking that the configuration does not block, or a blocking one presented as optional; long work left unwatched as the way to do it. Do NOT judge style, length or completeness: a short file that says nothing wrong passes. When failing it, quote each passage and PROPOSE the text that replaces it.

## Declaring it

```yaml
gates:
  - name: guidance-honored
    on: [doc]
    measures: judgment
```
